title: Reduce the R439 packet adapter to one dirty buffer
body:
PR2481 routes an ordinary R439 update through two restored dirty payload banks. This contribution uses one: exchange the source into the bank, route it into the target layout, update the target through a charged owned-record scan, reverse the routes and exchange back. Snapshot taps keep their source immutable.

For the exact 303 ordinary events and ten taps, route calls remain **1,232**, while exchanges fall **1,232 → 626** and outer packet XOR work falls **4,009 → 2,191** P-record units. The written proof covers arbitrary correlated bit payloads and invertible coordinate permutations under the explicit route/scan contract. The role/direction route multiset is unchanged; equal weighted route work additionally requires context-independent route tariffs. Physical headers, control, private child scratch and complete supplier admission remain open. This is not a bank minimum or new kappa.

The source-bound GL2(Z/9) replay covers all 431,568 family records in each direction, including 422,577 unowned records, all 313 event boundaries, and eight semantic faults. A separately implemented S3 check covers 216 chart triples and 2,592 event boundaries with seven faults, including noncommuting factor order. A separate specialist also reviewed the proof and reran the stable primary verifier under Python 3.14.6; that replay is explicitly distinguished from the independent small implementation.

Validation completed locally:
- Registered CPython 3.12 replay and source/metadata checks.
- All 15 retained and three live source corruptions rejected; changed cost receipt rejected.
- Optimized read-only, Git-free export replay, with unchanged bytes.
- Full PR2481 predecessor payload reproduced; six finite route counters agree in both directions.
- Selected-record integrity check passed; selected cold replay was not run because no selected construction changed.

Only `research/r439-one-buffer-packet/` is added. Base canonical main is `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4; exact freshness/overlap coverage and limitations are in TASK.json. The canonical claim is [Discussion2401](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2401#discussioncomment-18949757).

Credit ywz65's PR2481 (`d3ec95362a071e2726c5ff4ce587de80c7d4f984`), Ross Richardson's PR2448/2407/2437, Jose Manuel's PR2195, alephnan's PR1627/540, and the retained supplier/exporter lineage. The exchange and conjugation identities are standard; the contribution is the changed schedule, explicit contract/invoice and exact chronological binding. Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including a separate mathematical specialist. Apache-2.0; no independent human review, formal-kernel proof or hosted-CI success claimed.
